title: Genitive: Taigh a' bhalaich
question: What does 'taigh a' bhalaich' mean?
explanation: In the genitive the possessor follows the noun: 'taigh a' bhalaich' = 'the boy's house' ('balach' becomes 'balaich'). 'Taigh nam balach' would be 'the boys' house'.

title: Genitive: Bean an fhir
question: What does 'bean an fhir' mean?
explanation: 'Fear' becomes 'fhir' in the genitive after 'an': 'bean an fhir' = 'the man's wife'. 'Fear na mnà' would be 'the woman's husband'.

title: Possessive vs Genitive
question: What is the difference? 'Mo bhràthair' vs 'bràthair an fhir'
correct: First is my brother, second is the man's brother
wrong1: First is the man's brother, second is my brother
explanation: 'Mo bhràthair' (possessive) means 'my brother'; 'bràthair an fhir' (genitive) means 'the man's brother'.

title: Preposition: Ann an Glaschu
question: What does 'ann an Glaschu' mean?
explanation: 'Ann an' + place name indicates location: 'ann an Glaschu' = 'in Glasgow'.

title: Preposition: Aig an taigh
question: What does 'aig an taigh' mean?
explanation: 'Aig' means 'at': 'aig an taigh' = 'at the house'. 'Anns an taigh' would be 'in the house'.

title: Past: Chuala mi an cù
question: What does 'chuala mi an cù' mean?
explanation: 'Chuala' is the irregular past tense of 'cluinn' (hear). The subject 'mi' comes first, then the object: 'chuala mi an cù' = 'I heard the dog'.

title: Past: Bhuail
question: How do you say 'I hit' (past tense)?
explanation: The past tense lenites the verb: 'bhuail mi' = 'I hit'. 'Buail mi' is the bare command 'hit me', 'buailidh mi' is future and 'bhuaileadh mi' is conditional.

title: Future: Buailidh
question: How do you say 'I will hit'?
explanation: The future adds -idh and does not lenite: 'buailidh mi' = 'I will hit'. 'Bhuail mi' is past and 'bhuaileadh mi' is conditional.

title: Conditional: Bhuaileadh
question: What does 'Bhuaileadh e' mean?
explanation: The conditional lenites the verb and adds -eadh: 'bhuaileadh e' = 'he would hit'.

title: Imperative singular: Buail!
question: What does 'Buail!' mean when you speak to one friend?
explanation: The imperative singular is the bare verbal root: 'Buail!' = 'Hit!'

title: Imperative plural: Buailibh
question: What does 'Buailibh!' mean?
explanation: The plural imperative adds -ibh: 'Buailibh!' = 'Hit!' (to several people). 'Buailidh sibh' is the future, 'you will hit'.

title: Aspect: Simple past vs continuous
question: What is the difference between 'Dh'ith mi' and 'Bha mi ag ithe'?
correct: First is completed (I ate), second is ongoing (I was eating)
wrong1: First is ongoing (I was eating), second is completed (I ate)
wrong2: First is future (I will eat), second is present (I am eating)
wrong3: First is a question, second is a statement
explanation: 'Dh'ith mi' (I ate) is perfective; 'bha mi ag ithe' (I was eating) is imperfective.

title: Past: Thuirt
question: What does 'Thuirt mi' mean?
explanation: 'Thuirt' is the irregular past of 'abair' (say): 'thuirt mi' = 'I said'. 'Their mi' is 'I will say'.

title: Reported speech: Gun
question: What does 'gun' mean in 'Thuirt mi gun robh e sgìth'?
explanation: 'Gun' introduces what was said: 'thuirt mi gun robh e sgìth' = 'I said that he was tired'. The negative is 'nach': 'thuirt mi nach robh e sgìth'.

title: Reported speech: Nach
question: How do you say 'I said that he was not tired'?
correct: Thuirt mi nach robh e sgìth
wrong1: Thuirt mi gun robh e sgìth
wrong2: Thuirt mi cha robh e sgìth
wrong3: Thuirt mi nach eil e sgìth
explanation: After 'thuirt mi', a negative clause is introduced by 'nach': 'nach robh e sgìth' = 'that he was not tired'. 'Gun robh' would be positive, and 'nach eil' is present.

title: Ordinal: An treas
question: What does 'an treas' mean?
explanation: 'An treas' = 'the third' ('a' chiad' is first, 'an dàrna' second, 'an ceathramh' fourth).

title: Comparative: Nas motha
question: What does 'nas motha' mean?
explanation: 'Nas' creates the comparative: 'nas motha' = 'bigger'.

title: Superlative: As motha
question: What does 'as motha' mean?
explanation: 'As' creates the superlative: 'as motha' = 'biggest'.

title: Comparative: Nas fheàrr
question: What does 'nas fheàrr' mean?
explanation: 'Nas fheàrr' is the comparative of 'math' (good).

title: Superlative: As fheàrr
question: What does 'as fheàrr' mean?
explanation: 'As fheàrr' is the superlative of 'math' (good).

title: Negative question: Nach eil e ann?
question: What does 'Nach eil e ann?' mean?
explanation: 'Nach eil' begins a negative question: 'Nach eil e ann?' = 'Isn't he there?'

title: Negation: Gu dearbh
question: What does 'gu dearbh' mean?
explanation: 'Gu dearbh' emphasizes affirmation: 'Tha, gu dearbh' = 'Yes, indeed'.

title: Emphasis: Tusa
question: Which is the emphatic form of 'thu' (you, singular)?
explanation: Emphatic pronouns add an ending: mi becomes mise, thu becomes tusa, e becomes esan and sibh becomes sibhse.

title: Relative past: A bha
question: What does 'an duine a bha ann' mean?
wrong2: The man who will be there
wrong3: The man who is not there
explanation: 'A bha' is the past relative form: 'an duine a bha ann' = 'the man who was there'.

title: Relative future: A bhios
question: What does 'an duine a bhios ann' mean?
correct: The man who will be there
wrong2: The man who would be there
wrong3: The man who is not there
explanation: 'A bhios' is the future relative: 'an duine a bhios ann' = 'the man who will be there'.

title: Conjunction: Gus an
question: What does 'gus an' mean in 'Fuirich gus an till mi' (Wait ... I return)?
explanation: 'Gus an' means 'until' here (it can also mean 'so that'): 'fuirich gus an till mi' = 'wait until I return'.

title: Temporal: Nuair a
question: What does 'nuair a' mean?
explanation: 'Nuair a' introduces a temporal clause: 'nuair a thàinig e' = 'when he came'.

title: Conditional: Nan robh
question: What does 'nan robh mi ann' mean?
correct: If I were there (contrary to fact)
explanation: 'Nan robh' is the conditional ('if'), expressing contrary-to-fact scenarios.

title: Past: Thug
question: What does 'thug mi leabhar dha' mean?
wrong3: I will give him a book
explanation: 'Thug' is the past of 'thoir' (give): 'thug mi leabhar dha' = 'I gave him a book'. 'Dha' means 'to him' and 'dhi' means 'to her'.

title: Past: Chuir
question: What does 'chuir mi an leabhar air a' bhòrd' mean?
correct: I put the book on the table
wrong1: I took the book off the table
wrong2: I saw the book on the table
wrong3: I will put the book on the table
explanation: 'Chuir' is the past of 'cuir' (put), and 'air' means 'on'. 'Cur' is the verbal noun.

title: Plural agreement: Na taighean mòra
question: How do you say 'the big houses'?
explanation: An adjective after a plural noun usually adds -a: 'mòr' becomes 'mòra', so 'na taighean mòra' = 'the big houses'.

title: Consonant lenition rule
question: Which consonants lenite in Gaelic?
correct: B, C, D, F, G, M, P, S, T
explanation: Lenition affects: B→bh, C→ch, D→dh, F→fh, G→gh, M→mh, P→ph, S→sh, T→th.

title: Lenition: After the article
question: How do you say 'the sun' (grian is feminine)?
explanation: A feminine noun beginning with b, c, g, m or p is lenited after the article, which becomes a': 'a' ghrian'.

title: Prepositional + article fusion
question: What does 'den' mean?
explanation: 'Den' is the fusion of 'de' (of, off) + 'an' (the): 'thuit e den chathair' = 'he fell off the chair'.
